record.paper_title: Problèmes ouverts en théorie des intersections
record.original_question: If no regularity hypothesis is imposed on Y, even when X and Y are of finite type over the complex numbers and f:X→Y is a regular immersion of codimension 1, can one nevertheless construct a cohomological Gysin homomorphism with reasonable properties, in particular one that makes the Riemann-Roch comparison square (6.3) commute?

evidence.quote: Lorsqu'on ne fait pas d'hypothèse de régularité sur Y, et même si X et Y sont de type fini sur le corps C, on ne voit plus de définition plausible d'un homomorphisme de Gysin cohomologique (6.2), même pour une immersion régulière de codimension 1.
Peut-on en trouver un néanmoins avec des propriétés raisonnables, en particulier rendant commutatif le carré (6.3) ?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a regular closed immersion of codimension $1$ between schemes of finite type over $\mathbb{C}$. Assume no regularity (smoothness or non-singularity) hypothesis on $Y$. 

Recall that for $f$ a regular immersion between smooth varieties one has a cohomological Gysin homomorphism
$$f^{!}_{\mathrm{coh}} : H^{*}(X) \longrightarrow H^{*+2}(Y)$$
(where $H^{*}$ denotes a suitable cohomology theory, e.g. singular cohomology of the associated analytic space, or $\ell$-adic/Betti/Hodge cohomology), and a $K$-theoretic Gysin homomorphism
$$f^{!}_{K} : K_{0}(X) \longrightarrow K_{0}(Y),$$
related to one another, via the Chern character $\mathrm{ch}$ and the Todd class, by a commutative Riemann–Roch comparison square
$$
\begin{array}{ccc}
K_{0}(X) & \xrightarrow{\;f^{!}_{K}\;} & K_{0}(Y) \\
\downarrow{\scriptstyle \mathrm{ch}(-)\cdot \mathrm{Td}(X)} & & \downarrow{\scriptstyle \mathrm{ch}(-)\cdot \mathrm{Td}(Y)} \\
H^{*}(X) & \xrightarrow{\;f^{!}_{\mathrm{coh}}\;} & H^{*+2}(Y).
\end{array}
$$

Question: When $Y$ is allowed to be singular (only of finite type over $\mathbb{C}$), can one construct a cohomological Gysin homomorphism $f^{!}_{\mathrm{coh}}$ with reasonable functorial properties such that the above Riemann–Roch comparison square remains commutative? Equivalently, give a plausible definition of such a homomorphism, or prove that no such well-behaved construction can exist.
artifact.status_search_result: Modern developments (notably work on Gysin morphisms for regular immersions in motivic homotopy theory, including extensions of Gabber's construction, and Riemann–Roch results for homotopy invariant K-theory and projective local complete intersection morphisms over noetherian schemes without smoothness assumptions) provide partial cohomological Gysin maps for regular immersions allowing singular targets. However, it is not clear from publicly available sources that the specific question — producing a cohomological Gysin homomorphism on classical cohomology of singular complex varieties making the explicit Riemann–Roch comparison square commute for codimension-1 regular immersions into arbitrary singular targets — has been settled in the form originally posed. Status is best classified as unknown.

status_evidence.title: Riemann-Roch for homotopy invariant K-theory and Gysin morphisms
status_evidence.snippet: Construction of Gysin morphisms for regular immersions in cohomologies represented by spectra; Riemann-Roch for projective lci morphisms between finite-dimensional noetherian schemes without smoothness assumptions.
status_evidence.claim: Provides Gysin morphisms for regular immersions and a Riemann–Roch comparison without smoothness hypotheses, partially addressing the question in a motivic-spectral framework.

status_evidence.title: Topological Gysin Coherence for Algebraic Characteristic Classes of Singular Spaces
status_evidence.snippet: Framework of Gysin coherent characteristic classes formalizing Verdier–Riemann–Roch type formulae with respect to Gysin restriction for singular complex algebraic varieties.
status_evidence.claim: Gives a Verdier–Riemann–Roch type Gysin framework for singular complex varieties, but only for transverse intersection with smooth varieties.
